key_insight: HATCH lets an LLM create its own hints during training, then gradually downweights hinted trajectories to avoid over-relying on assisted solutions and improve unguided reasoning.
engineering_relevance: The method targets a practical failure mode in RL-style LLM training for math: when hard problems produce only wrong rollouts, self-generated hints can recover learning signal without requiring external supervision at inference time.
method: Train one policy to both solve queries and generate hints that help re-solve failed queries.
Use online weighting to anneal the impact of hinted trajectories and reduce hinted reward shift.
Apply gradient projection so hint-generation updates do not interfere with direct query-solving improvements.
evidence_signal: On mathematical reasoning benchmarks, HATCH outperforms prior methods by 1.02 pp on Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, 2.84 pp on Qwen3-1.7B, and 4.32 pp on Qwen3-8B.
watch_item: Because hinting and solving share one policy, the approach may be sensitive to how annealing and gradient projection are tuned, especially if hinted trajectories dominate early training.
paper_title: Teach to Learn: Hint Annealing for Self-improving LLM Reasoning
